description: Say goodbye to setup.py! Learn how to use the modern pyproject.toml standard to manage build systems, pin dependencies with lock files, and automate versioning.

slides.title: The End of setup.py
slides.content:
# A New Standard 📜

For 15 years, Python developers configured their projects using a file called `setup.py`.

The problem? `setup.py` was an *executable Python script*. Running it to install a package could theoretically run malicious code or fail depending on the user's Python version.

In PEP 518, Python introduced **`pyproject.toml`**: a static, declarative configuration file that replaces `setup.py`, `requirements.txt`, and config files like `flake8.ini`.

slides.title: Anatomy of pyproject.toml
slides.content:
# The `[build-system]` Table 🏗️

The most important part of `pyproject.toml` is the build system. 

Historically, `setuptools` was the only way to build Python packages. Now, you can explicitly tell `pip` which tool to use (e.g., Poetry, Flit, Hatch) before it attempts to build your code!

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core>=1.0.0"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"
```

slides.title: Project Metadata
slides.content:
# The `[project]` Table 📋

Instead of passing arguments to a `setup()` function, you declare your project metadata statically.

```toml
[project]
name = "my_awesome_app"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "An application that does things."
authors = [{name = "Jane Doe", email = "jane@doe.com"}]
requires-python = ">=3.9"

# Your actual dependencies!
dependencies = [
    "requests >=2.25.0",
    "flask >=2.0.0"
]
```

slides.title: Tool Configuration
slides.content:
# The `[tool]` Table 🛠️

Instead of having 10 different config files in your repository (`.pylintrc`, `.flake8`, `pytest.ini`), you can put all tool configurations in this one file!

```toml
[tool.black]
line-length = 88
target-version = ['py310']

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "-ra -q"
testpaths = [
    "tests",
]
```

slides.title: TOML Quiz
slides.content: Check your understanding of the modern standard.
slides.quizQuestion: Why did the Python community replace `setup.py` with `pyproject.toml`?
quizOptions: Because TOML files execute faster than Python files.
Because `setup.py` was executable code, whereas `pyproject.toml` is a safe, static, declarative file that allows explicit declaration of the required build system.
Because Microsoft bought Python and forced the change.

slides.title: Dependency Management
slides.content:
# The Problem with `>=` 💣

In our `pyproject.toml`, we specified `requests >=2.25.0`.

If you deploy your app today, it might install `2.26.0`. If you deploy it tomorrow, it might install `2.30.0`. 

If `2.30.0` introduces a breaking change, your production app will crash unexpectedly, even though you didn't change any of your own code! This is the nightmare of unpinned dependencies.

slides.title: Version Pinning
slides.content:
# Exact Versions 📌

To prevent this, we must use **Version Pinning** (e.g., `requests ==2.26.0`). 

However, manually finding and pinning exact versions for your dependencies (and all of *their* sub-dependencies!) is impossible.

We solve this using **Lock Files**.

slides.title: Lock Files
slides.content:
# `poetry.lock` 🔒

When you use Poetry (or `pipenv`), it reads your `pyproject.toml`, calculates the exact, perfectly compatible versions of every single package and sub-package required, and writes them to a `poetry.lock` file.

```text
# poetry.lock (Auto-generated, do not edit manually!)
[[package]]
name = "requests"
version = "2.26.0"

[[package]]
name = "urllib3" # A sub-dependency of requests
version = "1.26.7"
```

You commit `poetry.lock` to git. When you deploy, the server installs exactly what is in the lock file. Deterministic, crash-free deployments!

slides.title: The Traditional Way
slides.content:
# `pip-compile` 🛠️

If you aren't using Poetry, you can achieve lock files using the standard `pip-tools` library.

You create a simple `requirements.in` file:
`flask>=2.0`

Then you run `pip-compile`.
It calculates the exact hashes and sub-dependencies and generates a massive, pinned `requirements.txt` file automatically!

*(This is the professional way to use requirements.txt!)*

slides.title: Dependencies Quiz
slides.content: Test your knowledge of deterministic builds.
slides.quizQuestion: What is the primary purpose of a Lock File (like `poetry.lock`)?
quizOptions: It encrypts your source code so competitors cannot read it.
It permanently pins the exact version of every dependency (and sub-dependency) so that your application installs identically on every machine, preventing unexpected breaks from upstream updates.
It locks the database to prevent concurrent write errors.
It prevents users from uninstalling the application.

slides.title: Version Bumping
slides.content:
# Automating Releases 📈

When you release a new feature, you must bump the version in `pyproject.toml` from `1.2.0` to `1.3.0`.

If that version number is also hardcoded in your `__init__.py` and your documentation, changing it manually everywhere leads to mistakes.

Tools like `bumpversion` (or `bump2version`) automate this using RegEx.

slides.title: Using bumpversion
slides.content:
# `bumpversion` in Action 🤖

You define a `.bumpversion.cfg` file telling the tool where the version string lives.

```bash
# Automatically increments the 'minor' version (1.2.0 -> 1.3.0)
# It updates pyproject.toml, __init__.py, AND creates a git commit and git tag automatically!
bumpversion minor
```

This is essential for CI/CD pipelines!

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Build Master! 🎉

You've learned the modern standard for configuring Python.

## Key Takeaways

- ✅ **`pyproject.toml`:** The static, declarative replacement for `setup.py`. It holds build settings, project metadata, and tool configs (`[tool.black]`).
- ✅ **Version Pinning:** Using `>=` in production is dangerous. You must use exact `==` versions to ensure deterministic deployments.
- ✅ **Lock Files:** Use Poetry (or `pip-compile`) to automatically generate lock files that pin the exact versions of all sub-dependencies.
- ✅ **`bumpversion`:** Automate the tedious process of incrementing version numbers across your entire repository.
